articles.title: Global Inflation Outlook: Are We Past the Peak?

paragraphs.en: Global inflation has shown signs of meaningful deceleration over the past quarter, with headline CPI across G10 economies falling from an average of 4.2% to 3.1%. Core inflation, however, remains stickier than anticipated, particularly in the services sector where wage growth continues to exert upward pressure. Our models suggest that the 'last mile' of disinflation will be the most challenging, with central banks likely to maintain restrictive policy rates through at least Q3 2026.
paragraphs.zh: 过去一个季度，全球通胀显示出显著的减速迹象，G10经济体的总体CPI平均值从4.2%降至3.1%。然而，核心通胀比预期更具粘性，特别是在服务业领域，工资增长继续施加上行压力。我们的模型表明，去通胀的'最后一英里'将最具挑战性，央行可能在2026年第三季度之前维持限制性政策利率。

paragraphs.en: In the United States, the Fed's preferred PCE measure is projected to reach 2.4% by year-end, still above the 2% target but down materially from its peak. The labor market has cooled to a more sustainable pace, with job openings per unemployed worker falling to 1.2, close to pre-pandemic levels. This gives the FOMC room to deliver two 25bp cuts in H2 2026, in our view, though the timing remains data-dependent.
paragraphs.zh: 在美国，美联储偏好的PCE指标预计在年底前达到2.4%，仍高于2%的目标，但较峰值大幅下降。劳动力市场已降温至更可持续的节奏，每个失业者的职位空缺降至1.2，接近疫情前水平。我们认为，这为FOMC在2026年下半年进行两次25个基点的降息提供了空间，不过时机仍取决于数据。

paragraphs.en: The Eurozone presents a more complex picture. While energy prices have stabilized, services inflation remains elevated at 4.1%, driven by strong wage negotiations in Germany and France. The ECB faces a delicate balancing act: easing too early risks re-igniting price pressures, while waiting too long could unnecessarily depress growth. We expect the ECB to hold rates at 2.75% until at least September 2026.
paragraphs.zh: 欧元区的情况更为复杂。虽然能源价格已经稳定，但在德国和法国强劲工资谈判的推动下，服务业通胀仍高达4.1%。欧洲央行面临微妙的平衡：过早放松政策可能重新点燃价格压力，而等待过久可能不必要地压低增长。我们预计欧洲央行至少在2026年9月之前将利率维持在2.75%。

paragraphs.en: Key risk to watch: a resurgence in commodity prices driven by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East could upend the disinflation narrative. Our commodity strategists assign a 25% probability to Brent crude reaching $95/bbl by Q4 2026, which would add approximately 0.6pp to headline inflation across major economies.
paragraphs.zh: 需要关注的关键风险：中东地缘政治紧张局势推动的大宗商品价格反弹可能颠覆去通胀的叙事。我们的大宗商品策略师认为，布伦特原油在2026年第四季度达到95美元/桶的概率为25%，这将为主要经济体的总体通胀增加约0.6个百分点。

articles.recap_en: Goldman Sachs sees global inflation decelerating but the 'last mile' to 2% will be toughest due to sticky services inflation. Two Fed cuts expected in H2 2026; ECB likely on hold until September. Key tail risk is a commodity price spike from Middle East tensions.
articles.recap_zh: 高盛认为全球通胀正在放缓，但由于服务业通胀粘性，通往2%的'最后一英里'将最为艰难。预计美联储将在2026年下半年降息两次；欧洲央行可能在9月前按兵不动。关键尾部风险是中东紧张局势引发的大宗商品价格飙升。

articles.title: FX Strategy: Positioning for a Weaker Dollar in H2 2026

paragraphs.en: The US Dollar has entered a structural softening phase, driven by narrowing rate differentials and a deteriorating fiscal outlook. The DXY index has declined 4.2% from its March highs, and our quantitative models point to further depreciation of 3-5% through year-end. This is not a cyclical blip but reflects a fundamental reassessment of US assets by global reserve managers.
paragraphs.zh: 美元已进入结构性走软阶段，受利差收窄和财政前景恶化的推动。DXY指数已从3月高点下跌4.2%，我们的量化模型显示到年底将进一步贬值3-5%。这不是周期性波动，而是反映了全球储备管理者对美国资产的基本面重新评估。

paragraphs.en: The widening US fiscal deficit, projected to reach 7.2% of GDP in FY2026, is eroding the dollar's safe-haven premium. Foreign official holdings of US Treasuries have declined for five consecutive quarters, with China and Japan reducing their positions by a combined $180 billion over the past 12 months. This trend is likely to accelerate as BRICS+ countries expand their local-currency settlement mechanisms.
paragraphs.zh: 美国财政赤字不断扩大，预计2026财年将达到GDP的7.2%，正在侵蚀美元的避险溢价。外国官方持有美国国债已连续五个季度下降，中国和日本在过去12个月中合计减持1800亿美元。随着金砖国家扩大本币结算机制，这一趋势可能会加速。

paragraphs.en: Our top FX recommendations for H2 2026: (1) Long EUR/USD — target 1.18, driven by improving Eurozone growth and ECB patience; (2) Long JPY — target 135, as the BoJ continues its normalization path with two additional 15bp hikes expected; (3) Long MXN — target 16.8, benefiting from nearshoring tailwinds and attractive carry at 9.5% policy rate.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对2026年下半年的首要外汇建议：(1) 做多欧元/美元——目标价1.18，受欧元区增长改善和欧洲央行耐心的推动；(2) 做多日元——目标价135，因日本央行继续推进正常化路径，预计再加息两次各15个基点；(3) 做多墨西哥比索——目标价16.8，受益于近岸外包的顺风和高达9.5%政策利率的吸引力。

articles.recap_en: JPMorgan calls for structural USD weakness with 3-5% further depreciation by year-end, driven by fiscal concerns and BRICS+ de-dollarization. Top picks: long EUR/USD, long JPY, long MXN. Key for interviews: understand the link between US fiscal trajectory and dollar reserve status.
articles.recap_zh: 摩根大通认为美元将结构性走弱，年底前将进一步贬值3-5%，受财政担忧和金砖国家去美元化推动。首选交易：做多欧元/美元、做多日元、做多墨西哥比索。面试关键：理解美国财政轨迹与美元储备地位之间的联系。

articles.title: How Much Power Do Data Centers Really Need?

paragraphs.en: The surge in AI-driven demand for data center capacity has triggered an unprecedented expansion cycle in the power sector. Our analysis indicates that US data center electricity consumption will grow from 21 GW in 2024 to 52 GW by 2030, representing a compound annual growth rate of 16%. This implies data centers will account for 9% of total US electricity demand by 2030, up from 4% today.
paragraphs.zh: AI驱动的数据中心容量需求激增，引发了电力行业前所未有的扩建周期。我们的分析表明，美国数据中心电力消费将从2024年的21吉瓦增长到2030年的52吉瓦，复合年增长率为16%。这意味着数据中心将在2030年占美国总电力需求的9%，而目前为4%。

paragraphs.en: This demand growth has profound implications across the energy value chain. Independent power producers (IPPs) with existing gas-fired assets — such as Vistra, NRG, and Calpine — are best positioned to capture near-term value, as they can sign premium-priced 24/7 power purchase agreements (PPAs) with hyperscalers. We estimate these PPAs command a 25-35% premium over wholesale market prices, reflecting the value of reliability guarantees.
paragraphs.zh: 这种需求增长对整个能源价值链产生了深远影响。拥有现有燃气发电资产的独立电力生产商——如Vistra、NRG和Calpine——最有能力捕捉近期价值，因为它们可以与超大规模客户签订溢价24/7购电协议。我们估计这些购电协议的价格比批发市场价格高出25-35%，反映了可靠性保证的价值。

paragraphs.en: The nuclear renaissance narrative deserves scrutiny. While tech companies have announced ambitious deals for nuclear power — including Microsoft's agreement to revive Three Mile Island and Google's partnership with Kairos Power on small modular reactors (SMRs) — the timelines extend well beyond 2030. For investors, the near-term story remains natural gas, which is the only source that can reliably deliver the 24/7 baseload power that data centers require at scale.
paragraphs.zh: 核能复兴的叙事值得仔细审视。虽然科技公司已经宣布了雄心勃勃的核能交易——包括微软重启三哩岛核电站的协议，以及谷歌与Kairos Power在小堆上的合作——但时间线远超2030年。对投资者而言，近期的主线仍然是天然气，它是唯一能够可靠提供数据中心所需的大规模24/7基荷电力的能源。

articles.recap_en: Morgan Stanley projects US data center power demand more than doubling to 52 GW by 2030 (16% CAGR). Gas-fired IPPs are the near-term winners with 25-35% PPA premiums. Nuclear hype is real but timelines stretch past 2030 — natural gas is the practical baseload solution for now.
articles.recap_zh: 摩根士丹利预计美国数据中心电力需求到2030年将翻倍以上至52吉瓦（年复合增长率16%）。燃气独立电力生产商是近期赢家，购电协议溢价25-35%。核能热度真实存在但时间线超过2030年——天然气是当前最实际的基荷解决方案。

articles.title: Reshoring and Supply Chain Transformation: A Multi-Decade Theme

paragraphs.en: The reconfiguration of global supply chains is not a transitory post-pandemic adjustment — it is a multi-decade structural theme reshaping industrial geography. Our research identifies three primary drivers: (1) geopolitical de-risking, particularly the US-China strategic competition; (2) policy incentives, including $52 billion in CHIPS Act grants and $120 billion in IRA clean energy tax credits; and (3) technology-driven manufacturing automation that reduces the labor-cost advantage of offshore production.
paragraphs.zh: 全球供应链的重构不是一次性的疫后调整——它是一个重塑工业地理格局的跨十年结构性主题。我们的研究识别出三个主要驱动因素：(1) 地缘政治去风险化，特别是中美战略竞争；(2) 政策激励，包括520亿美元的芯片法案拨款和1200亿美元的IRA清洁能源税收抵免；(3) 技术驱动的制造业自动化，降低了离岸生产的劳动力成本优势。

paragraphs.en: The scale of industrial investment is remarkable. US manufacturing construction spending has increased from $75 billion annually in 2019 to over $210 billion in 2025, with computer/electronic/electrical manufacturing accounting for the largest share. Mexico has emerged as the primary nearshoring beneficiary, with FDI inflows reaching $45 billion in 2025, concentrated in automotive, electronics, and aerospace.
paragraphs.zh: 工业投资的规模令人瞩目。美国制造业建设支出已从2019年的每年750亿美元增加到2025年的超过2100亿美元，其中计算机/电子/电气制造占据最大份额。墨西哥已成为近岸外包的主要受益者，2025年FDI流入达到450亿美元，集中在汽车、电子和航空航天领域。

paragraphs.en: Our top stock picks for this theme: (1) Eaton (ETN) — electrical infrastructure for new factories and data centers; (2) Rockwell Automation (ROK) — factory automation and digital transformation; (3) Prologis (PLD) — logistics real estate for reconfigured distribution networks; (4) Quanta Services (PWR) — power grid expansion and hardening; (5) TFI International (TFII) — cross-border logistics benefiting from Mexico nearshoring.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对该主题的首选股票：(1) 伊顿(ETN)——为新工厂和数据中心提供电气基础设施；(2) 罗克韦尔自动化(ROK)——工厂自动化和数字化转型；(3) 安博(PLD)——为重新配置的分销网络提供物流地产；(4) Quanta Services(PWR)——电网扩建和强化；(5) TFI International(TFII)——受益于墨西哥近岸外包的跨境物流。

articles.recap_en: Citi frames supply chain reconfiguration as a multi-decade theme driven by geopolitics, policy (CHIPS Act + IRA), and automation. US manufacturing construction spending up ~3x since 2019. Top picks: ETN, ROK, PLD, PWR, TFII. Know the three drivers and the Mexico nearshoring angle for interviews.
articles.recap_zh: 花旗将供应链重构视为由地缘政治、政策（芯片法案+通胀削减法案）和自动化驱动的跨十年主题。美国制造业建设支出自2019年以来增长约3倍。首选：伊顿、罗克韦尔、安博、Quanta Services、TFI International。面试要点：了解三大驱动因素和墨西哥近岸外包角度。

articles.title: Institute Insights

paragraphs.en:
Institute Insights




17 May 2026




 

Under the big top, the economy is juggling many balancing acts. This week, Bank of America Institute invites you to step right up and see how consumers are performing; where summer travel is heading; as well as the thrills and chills of AI’s impact on the labor market.

The US consumer is the ringleader for economic growth: Bank of America credit and debit card data shows spending growth was up 4.8% year-over-year (YoY) in April, reaching the highest level in three years. And this strength holds even when stripping out gasoline spending. Although, in this three-ring circus, some consumers are facing a tightrope. For lower-income households, wages are no longer keeping pace with spending, whereas for higher income, wage growth remains above spending. This has led to lower‑ and middle‑income consumers easing back on discretionary “nice‑to‑have” categories like restaurants. While households still have some near‑term buffers – including tax refunds and savings – these too are unevenly distributed, underscoring the growing gap between headline resilience and stress experienced by some households. Read publications: Consumer Checkpoint: April showers and The Institute Employment Report: April 2026.

Summer travel remains a sensation this year, with the 2026 Bank of America Summer Travel Outlook finding that most travelers are adjusting – not canceling – their summer travel plans in response to higher gas prices. That said, airline transactions started to fall in April, and a "K-shaped" pattern has emerged this travel season. Lower-income households are much more likely to have no travel plans (nearly 40%), and Bank of America card data shows their travel-related spending growth is down so far in 2026. Popular destinations remain concentrated stateside – led by California, Florida, Texas and New York – while international travelers favor spots in Europe and other North American countries. Read publication: Summer Travel 2026: Resilient, but uneven.

AI is no longer a sideshow but has moved straight into the center ring of the labor market. As it becomes woven into everyday work, roughly a quarter of jobs are now exposed to generative AI – especially in higher‑income economies where non‑routine, cognitive tasks dominate. Still, BofA Global Research argues that how this act plays out depends less on AI itself and more on how well economies adapt, doing so through skill development and overall workforce quality. Rather than wiping jobs off the bill, AI will reshape how the acts are performed. That said, policy can help nudge firms toward responsible and inclusive AI use, so productivity gains are shared, instead of leaving some workers trapped in the tiger’s cage. Read publication: Adaptability is the new job security: AI and the future of work.

Liz Everett Krisberg

Head of Bank of America Institute

paragraphs.zh:
**机构洞察**

2026年5月17日

在大帐篷之下，经济正上演着多重平衡术。本周，美国银行研究所诚邀您亲临现场，一睹消费者如何表现、夏季旅游走向何方，以及人工智能对劳动力市场带来的刺激与寒意。

美国消费者是经济增长的"领班"：美国银行信用卡和借记卡数据显示，4月份消费支出同比增长4.8%，达到三年来最高水平。即便剔除汽油支出，这一增长势头依然强劲。然而，在这个"三环马戏团"中，部分消费者正面临走钢丝的困境。对于低收入家庭而言，工资增速已跟不上支出步伐；而高收入家庭的工资增长仍高于支出。这导致中低收入消费者在餐饮等"锦上添花"的非必需品类上有所收敛。尽管家庭仍有一些短期缓冲——包括退税和储蓄——但这些资源分布不均，凸显了总体韧性表象与部分家庭实际压力之间日益扩大的差距。请参阅报告：《消费者观察：四月阵雨》及《研究所就业报告：2026年4月》。

今年夏季旅游依然热度不减。2026年美国银行夏季旅游展望发现，面对油价上涨，多数旅行者选择调整而非取消出行计划。不过，航空交易量自4月起开始下滑，本旅游季呈现出"K型"分化格局。低收入家庭更可能完全没有旅行计划（近40%），美国银行信用卡数据显示，2026年迄今其旅游相关支出增长为负。热门目的地仍集中在国内——以加州、佛罗里达州、得克萨斯州和纽约州为首——而国际游客则青睐欧洲及其他北美国家。请参阅报告：《2026年夏季旅游：韧性犹存，但分化加剧》。

人工智能已不再是"配角"，而是直接步入劳动力市场的"中心舞台"。随着AI融入日常工作，约四分之一的岗位现已暴露于生成式AI的影响之下——尤其是在以非重复性认知任务为主导的高收入经济体中。不过，美国银行全球研究认为，这一"剧目"如何展开，更多取决于经济体通过技能开发和整体劳动力质量进行适应的能力，而非AI本身。AI不会让岗位"谢幕"，而是会重塑工作的执行方式。与此同时，政策可引导企业负责任且包容地使用AI，使生产力提升得以共享，避免部分劳动者被困于"虎笼"之中。请参阅报告：《适应力是新的工作保障：AI与工作的未来》。

Liz Everett Krisberg

David Michael Tinsley

**机构洞察**

2026年5月17日

在大帐篷之下，经济正上演着多重平衡术。本周，美国银行研究所诚邀您亲临现场，一睹消费者如何表现、夏季旅游走向何方，以及人工智能对劳动力市场带来的刺激与寒意。

美国消费者是经济增长的"领班"：美国银行信用卡和借记卡数据显示，4月份消费支出同比增长4.8%，达到三年来最高水平。即便剔除汽油支出，这一增长势头依然强劲。然而，在这个"三环马戏团"中，部分消费者正面临走钢丝的困境。对于低收入家庭而言，工资增速已跟不上支出步伐；而高收入家庭的工资增长仍高于支出。这导致中低收入消费者在餐饮等"锦上添花"的非必需品类上有所收敛。尽管家庭仍有一些短期缓冲——包括退税和储蓄——但这些资源分布不均，凸显了总体韧性表象与部分家庭实际压力之间日益扩大的差距。请参阅报告：《消费者观察：四月阵雨》及《研究所就业报告：2026年4月》。

今年夏季旅游依然热度不减。2026年美国银行夏季旅游展望发现，面对油价上涨，多数旅行者选择调整而非取消出行计划。不过，航空交易量自4月起开始下滑，本旅游季呈现出"K型"分化格局。低收入家庭更可能完全没有旅行计划（近40%），美国银行信用卡数据显示，2026年迄今其旅游相关支出增长为负。热门目的地仍集中在国内——以加州、佛罗里达州、得克萨斯州和纽约州为首——而国际游客则青睐欧洲及其他北美国家。请参阅报告：《2026年夏季旅游：韧性犹存，但分化加剧》。

人工智能已不再是"配角"，而是直接步入劳动力市场的"中心舞台"。随着AI融入日常工作，约四分之一的岗位现已暴露于生成式AI的影响之下——尤其是在以非重复性认知任务为主导的高收入经济体中。不过，美国银行全球研究认为，这一"剧目"如何展开，更多取决于经济体通过技能开发和整体劳动力质量进行适应的能力，而非AI本身。AI不会让岗位"谢幕"，而是会重塑工作的执行方式。与此同时，政策可引导企业负责任且包容地使用AI，使生产力提升得以共享，避免部分劳动者被困于"虎笼"之中。请参阅报告：《适应力是新的工作保障：AI与工作的未来》。

articles.recap_en: BofA’s April data shows headline consumer spending growth hit a three-year high of 4.8% YoY, but beneath the surface a K-shaped recovery is widening: lower-income households are pulling back on discretionary categories like restaurants, while higher-income spending remains robust. Summer travel is resilient but uneven, with airline transactions declining in April and nearly 40% of lower-income households having no travel plans, even as destinations like California and Florida remain popular. On AI, BofA estimates roughly a quarter of jobs are now exposed to generative AI, arguing the outcome hinges on workforce adaptability and policy, not automation alone—implying investors should watch for sector-specific productivity shifts rather than broad job displacement.
articles.recap_zh: 根据美国银行研究所2026年5月17日发布的报告，美国消费支出在4月同比增长4.8%，创三年新高，但低收家庭工资增速已落后于支出，被迫削减餐馆等可选消费，而高收家庭工资增长仍高于支出，凸显经济韧性下的结构性分化。夏季旅行方面，多数人因油价上涨调整而非取消计划，但航空交易量4月开始下降，近40%低收家庭无旅行安排，热门目的地仍集中在美国本土。人工智能正重塑劳动力市场，约四分之一岗位受生成式AI影响，尤其在认知型非 routine 工作为主的高收入经济体，但报告认为AI不会大规模取代就业，而是改变工作方式，政策应引导技能培训以促进包容性增长。

articles.title: Daily Insights: Lower-income wage growth barely keeps up with gas prices

paragraphs.en:
Lower-income wage growth barely keeps up with gas prices




Daily Insights | 18 May 2026




 

Lower-income households’ after-tax wage increases barely offset average increases in gas spending

After-tax wage and salary increase by household income tercile compared to average per household increase in gasoline spending (April 2026, seasonally adjusted, ratio)







Source: Bank of America internal data

Note: The difference in wages is based on the 3-month moving average while gas spending differences are monthly.

BANK OF AMERICA INSTITUTE

Both lower- and middle-income households have seen a slowdown in their discretionary spending growth since gas prices began rising in early March. One driver is “K-shaped” wage growth: according to Bank of America internal data, higher-income households’ after-tax wage growth reached 6.0% year-over-year (YoY) in April, compared to a more modest 1.5% YoY for lower income. This gap is the widest we’ve observed since our data series began in 2015.

Lower-income households’ smaller wage base, combined with slower growth, means their wage gains over the past year have only just covered higher gas spending. Meanwhile, higher-income groups’ wage increases have offset higher gas spending nearly seventeen-fold.

Read our publication: Consumer Checkpoint: April showers.

低收入群体薪资涨幅勉强跟上油价上涨步伐

每日洞察 | 2026年5月18日

低收入家庭税后工资增幅仅能勉强覆盖汽油支出平均增幅

按家庭收入三分位组划分的税后工资与薪金增幅对比家庭汽油支出平均增幅（2026年4月，经季节性调整，比率）

资料来源：美国银行内部数据
注：工资差异基于三个月移动平均值，汽油支出差异为月度数据。

美国银行研究所

自3月初油价开始上涨以来，中低收入家庭的可自由支配支出增长均有所放缓。其中一个驱动因素是"K型"薪资增长：根据美国银行内部数据，高收入家庭4月税后工资同比增幅达6.0%，而低收入家庭仅为1.5%。这一差距是我们自2015年数据序列启动以来观察到的最大值。

低收入家庭薪资基数较小，加之增长缓慢，意味着其过去一年的薪资增长仅能勉强覆盖汽油支出的增加。与此同时，高收入群体的薪资增长对汽油支出增加的覆盖倍数接近17倍。

articles.recap_en: According to a May 2026 Bank of America Institute report, lower-income households saw after-tax wage growth of only 1.5% year-over-year in April, barely enough to offset rising gas costs, while higher-income households enjoyed 6.0% wage growth—a record gap since 2015. This "K-shaped" recovery means higher-income groups have offset higher gas spending nearly seventeen-fold, whereas lower-income discretionary spending growth has already slowed since March. The implication is that consumer spending divergence will persist, potentially pressuring discount retailers and credit-dependent sectors while premium brands and services catering to higher earners remain resilient.
articles.recap_zh: 根据美国银行2026年5月18日发布的报告，低收入家庭税后工资增速仅为1.5%（同比），几乎被同期汽油支出上涨所抵消，而高收入家庭工资增速达6.0%，两者差距创2015年以来新高。这一“K型”工资增长导致中低收入家庭自3月油价上涨以来 discretionary spending 增速放缓。投资者需关注消费分化对零售、能源及必需消费品板块的潜在影响，低收入群体购买力承压可能抑制整体消费复苏。

articles.recap_en: The Barclays Eagle Eye newsletter highlights three key themes: rising bond yields driven by inflation pressures amid muddled politics from the Trump-Xi meeting and UK government turmoil; the growing popularity of prediction markets for forecasting event outcomes; and U.S. regulators moving closer to abolishing quarterly reporting requirements, though most companies are unlikely to drop the practice. Additionally, it notes that fears of AI disruption have hurt share prices in threatened sectors, but analysts see potential benefits from the disruption. For investors, the key implication is to monitor inflation-driven yield moves and consider how AI disruption may create opportunities despite initial market sell-offs.

paragraphs.en:
Sponsored by	


 


 


 


Bond Markets Are Bullying the U.K. and Japan. One Has the Right Defenses.


 


Plus, why Nvidia is underappreciated and secrets revealed in SpaceX’s IPO filing


 


By Aaron Back
paragraphs.zh:
主办方

债券市场正在施压英国与日本，其中一国拥有正确防御手段。

此外，英伟达为何被低估，以及SpaceX上市文件中披露的秘密

作者：Aaron Back

paragraphs.en: Bond Markets Are Bullying the U.K. and Japan. One Has the Right Defenses.
paragraphs.zh: 债券市场正在施压英国与日本，其中一国拥有正确的防御手段。

paragraphs.en: Plus, why Nvidia is underappreciated and secrets revealed in SpaceX’s IPO filing
paragraphs.zh: 此外，英伟达为何被低估，以及SpaceX首次公开募股文件中揭示的秘密。

paragraphs.en:
Good morning, I’m filling in for Spencer Jakab. Stocks appear headed for a muted open after yesterday’s strong showing. Another record quarter for Nvidia failed to excite investors, plus there was a slew of news about blockbuster IPOs from SpaceX and OpenAI. Oil prices edged lower after yesterday’s big slide on renewed hopes for an end to the Iran war. Treasury yields are subdued although they remain at elevated levels.



 



​📈 Follow our live markets data and coverage.



 


-	Last	Chg%


↑ S&P 500 FUTURES

	7,457.25	+0.07%


↑ DJIA FUTURES

	50,274.00	+0.36%


↓ NASDAQ 100 FUTURES

	29,382.50	-0.03%


↑ U.S. 10 YEAR TREASURY NOTE

	4.60	+0.20


↓ CRUDE OIL

	97.72	-0.55%


↓ GOLD

	4,533.60	-0.04%


 


5/21/2026, 6:28:04 AM ET


 


 


 


Dire straits


 



The U.K. and Japan appear to share many common problems at the moment. Both are great island nations that find themselves besieged by cranky bond markets, at risk of losing their fiscal credibility. 



 



Beneath the surface, Japan has much more going for it, and for investors.



 



Start with the similarities. Fiscal budgets, already stretched, are getting further strained by a combination of politics and the global energy crisis emanating from the Strait of Hormuz. Both nations’ government bonds and currencies are under pressure.



 



Since the Iran war began, 10-year government bond yields have jumped from 4.25% to 5.04% in the U.K., and from 2.12% to 2.78% in Japan. The yield on 30-year government bonds in Japan this week hit 4.13%, the highest level since they began being issued in 1999.



 



Japan’s Achilles’ heel in this situation is its dependence on foreign oil and gas. Japan imported 87% of its total energy supply in 2024, compared with 48% for the U.K., according to the International Energy Agency. 



 



For now, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi seems determined to shield the public from feeling too much of a squeeze, using subsidies to keep fuel prices low. Last week Takaichi asked the government to prepare a supplementary budget for fuel subsidies, something she previously insisted wasn’t necessary.



 



In a bear-case scenario, where Tokyo maintains the subsidies even as oil prices rise to $130 a barrel, providing that support could cost 2% of GDP, according to estimates from Capital Economics. 



 



But, compared with the U.K., Japan also has deep strengths. The first is political stability. What bond investors seem to fear most is that center-left Labour Prime Minister Keir Starmer will be replaced with a more-profligate, left-wing Labour leader.



 



Even worse, the right-wing-populist Reform party could ultimately be swept to power, with unpredictable consequences. By contrast, Takaichi in Japan remains popular and the hold of her Liberal Democratic Party on power is perhaps stronger now than ever.  



 



More important is the underlying strength of the Japanese economy and corporate sector. Japan occupies a crucial—and, especially compared with Taiwan and Korea—under appreciated role in the global supply chain for AI hardware.



 



This includes world-leading companies like semiconductor equipment-maker Tokyo Electron and memory-chip maker Kioxia Holdings. The country is also home to niche suppliers of things like ceramics and other advanced materials.



 



This helps explain why, despite all the bond-market turmoil, Japan’s Topix index is up 11% so far this year, compared with a 4% rise for the U.K.’s FTSE 100. The more tech-heavy Nikkei 225 has risen 19%, even outpacing the Nasdaq’s 12% gain. 



 



So the best investors can hope for in the U.K. is probably that the government will muddle through without succumbing to a political or fiscal collapse. By contrast, Japan offers the one thing all investors want: upside potential.



 





 




 


 



This is an edition of the Markets A.M. newsletter, preparing you for the trading day ahead with expert insight into the companies and industries set to move markets. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.



 


 


 


Stocks I’m Watching


 



↘️ Rocket Lab: Shares of the launch-and-satellite company, which has aimed to go toe-to-toe with SpaceX and other heavyweights in the space industry, fell more than 5% premarket after Elon Musk’s rocket company filed a prospectus for a stock offering that could raise $80 billion or more. Other space-based businesses, including Virgin Galactic and AST SpaceMobile, advanced.



 



↘️ Advanced Micro Devices: The chip maker is gearing up to invest more than $10 billion across Taiwan’s semiconductor sector to meet growing demand for AI infrastructure. Shares ticked down slightly.



 



↗️ Scottish Mortgage Investment Trust and Edinburgh Worldwide Investment Trust: Shares in the U.K. investment trusts, which have stakes in SpaceX, rose more than 2% after the rocket company’s Wednesday filing.



 



↘️ Intuit: The maker of TurboTax and QuickBooks plans to lay off 17% of its workforce as it remakes itself into an AI-first platform. Shares fell 12% premarket.



 



↗️ Samsung Electronics, LG Electronics, SK Hynix: South Korean semiconductor and electronics manufacturers’ stocks rallied, following strong quarterly results from Nvidia and comments from its CEO Jensen Huang on opportunities in “physical AI.” Samsung also benefited from an 11th-hour labor-dispute resolution that averted a crippling 18-day strike.
paragraphs.zh:
早上好，我今天临时替班斯宾塞·贾卡布。继昨日强劲表现后，美股今日开盘料将平淡。英伟达再创季度纪录新高却未能提振投资者情绪，此外SpaceX与OpenAI相继传出重磅IPO消息。受伊朗战争有望结束的预期推动，油价在昨日大幅下挫后今日小幅走低。国债收益率虽仍处高位，但已有所回落。

📈 关注我们的实时市场数据与报道。

- 最新价 涨跌幅
↑ 标普500期货 7,457.25 +0.07%
↑ 道指期货 50,274.00 +0.36%
↓ 纳斯达克100期货 29,382.50 -0.03%
↑ 美国10年期国债 4.60 +0.20
↓ 原油 97.72 -0.55%
↓ 黄金 4,533.60 -0.04%

2026年5月21日，美国东部时间上午6:28:04

困境重重

英国与日本当前似乎面临诸多共同难题。这两个伟大的岛国均遭债券市场围困，面临丧失财政信誉的风险。

表象之下，日本拥有更多利好因素，对投资者而言亦是如此。

先从相似之处说起。本就捉襟见肘的财政预算，因政治因素及霍尔木兹海峡引发的全球能源危机而进一步承压。两国国债与货币均面临压力。

自伊朗战争爆发以来，英国10年期国债收益率从4.25%跃升至5.04%，日本则从2.12%升至2.78%。本周日本30年期国债收益率触及4.13%，创1999年该期限国债发行以来最高水平。

在此背景下，日本的致命弱点在于其对海外石油与天然气的依赖。根据国际能源署数据，2024年日本能源总供应量的87%依赖进口，而英国这一比例为48%。

目前，首相高市早苗似乎决心通过补贴维持燃油低价，以减轻民众压力。上周，高市要求政府为燃油补贴编制补充预算，而她此前曾坚称此举并无必要。

根据凯投宏观的估算，在最悲观情景下，若东京方面在油价升至每桶130美元时仍维持补贴，相关支出可能高达GDP的2%。

但与英国相比，日本亦具备深厚优势。首先是政治稳定性。债券投资者最担忧的，似乎是中左翼工党首相基尔·斯塔默将被更挥霍无度的左翼工党领袖取代。

更糟的是，右翼民粹主义政党改革党最终可能上台执政，带来不可预测的后果。相比之下，日本的高市早苗仍广受欢迎，其自民党的执政地位或许比以往任何时候都更加稳固。

更为重要的是日本经济与企业部门的潜在实力。日本在全球人工智能硬件供应链中占据关键——且相较于台湾与韩国而言常被低估——的角色。

这包括半导体设备制造商东京电子与存储芯片制造商铠侠控股等世界领先企业。日本还拥有陶瓷及其他先进材料等细分领域的专业供应商。

这有助于解释为何尽管债市动荡，日本东证指数今年迄今仍上涨11%，而英国富时100指数仅上涨4%。科技股权重更高的日经225指数已上涨19%，甚至跑赢纳斯达克指数12%的涨幅。

因此，英国投资者最大的期望，或许是政府能在不陷入政治或财政崩溃的情况下勉力维持。相比之下，日本提供了所有投资者都渴望的东西：上行潜力。

本文为《市场早报》通讯内容，旨在通过专业洞察分析可能影响市场的企业与行业，助您迎接交易日。若尚未订阅，请点击此处订阅。

Another record quarter for Nvidia failed to excite investors, plus there was a slew of news about blockbuster IPOs from SpaceX and OpenAI. Oil prices edged lower after yesterday’s big slide on renewed hopes for an end to the Iran war. Treasury yields are subdued although they remain at elevated levels.

Dire straits


 



The U.K. and Japan appear to share many common problems at the moment. Both are great island nations that find themselves besieged by cranky bond markets, at risk of losing their fiscal credibility. 



 



Beneath the surface, Japan has much more going for it, and for investors.



 



Start with the similarities. Fiscal budgets, already stretched, are getting further strained by a combination of politics and the global energy crisis emanating from the Strait of Hormuz. Both nations’ government bonds and currencies are under pressure.



 



Since the Iran war began, 10-year government bond yields have jumped from 4.25% to 5.04% in the U.K., and from 2.12% to 2.78% in Japan. The yield on 30-year government bonds in Japan this week hit 4.13%, the highest level since they began being issued in 1999.



 



Japan’s Achilles’ heel in this situation is its dependence on foreign oil and gas. Japan imported 87% of its total energy supply in 2024, compared with 48% for the U.K., according to the International Energy Agency. 



 



For now, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi seems determined to shield the public from feeling too much of a squeeze, using subsidies to keep fuel prices low. Last week Takaichi asked the government to prepare a supplementary budget for fuel subsidies, something she previously insisted wasn’t necessary.



 



In a bear-case scenario, where Tokyo maintains the subsidies even as oil prices rise to $130 a barrel, providing that support could cost 2% of GDP, according to estimates from Capital Economics. 



 



But, compared with the U.K., Japan also has deep strengths. The first is political stability. What bond investors seem to fear most is that center-left Labour Prime Minister Keir Starmer will be replaced with a more-profligate, left-wing Labour leader.



 



Even worse, the right-wing-populist Reform party could ultimately be swept to power, with unpredictable consequences. By contrast, Takaichi in Japan remains popular and the hold of her Liberal Democratic Party on power is perhaps stronger now than ever.  



 



More important is the underlying strength of the Japanese economy and corporate sector. Japan occupies a crucial—and, especially compared with Taiwan and Korea—under appreciated role in the global supply chain for AI hardware.



 



This includes world-leading companies like semiconductor equipment-maker Tokyo Electron and memory-chip maker Kioxia Holdings. The country is also home to niche suppliers of things like ceramics and other advanced materials.



 



This helps explain why, despite all the bond-market turmoil, Japan’s Topix index is up 11% so far this year, compared with a 4% rise for the U.K.’s FTSE 100. The more tech-heavy Nikkei 225 has risen 19%, even outpacing the Nasdaq’s 12% gain. 



 



So the best investors can hope for in the U.K. is probably that the government will muddle through without succumbing to a political or fiscal collapse. By contrast, Japan offers the one thing all investors want: upside potential.



 





 




 


 



This is an edition of the Markets A.M. newsletter, preparing you for the trading day ahead with expert insight into the companies and industries set to move markets. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.



 


 


 


Stocks I’m Watching


 



↘️ Rocket Lab: Shares of the launch-and-satellite company, which has aimed to go toe-to-toe with SpaceX and other heavyweights in the space industry, fell more than 5% premarket after Elon Musk’s rocket company filed a prospectus for a stock offering that could raise $80 billion or more. Other space-based businesses, including Virgin Galactic and AST SpaceMobile, advanced.



 



↘️ Advanced Micro Devices: The chip maker is gearing up to invest more than $10 billion across Taiwan’s semiconductor sector to meet growing demand for AI infrastructure. Shares ticked down slightly.



 



↗️ Scottish Mortgage Investment Trust and Edinburgh Worldwide Investment Trust: Shares in the U.K. investment trusts, which have stakes in SpaceX, rose more than 2% after the rocket company’s Wednesday filing.



 



↘️ Intuit: The maker of TurboTax and QuickBooks plans to lay off 17% of its workforce as it remakes itself into an AI-first platform. Shares fell 12% premarket.



 



↗️ Samsung Electronics, LG Electronics, SK Hynix: South Korean semiconductor and electronics manufacturers’ stocks rallied, following strong quarterly results from Nvidia and comments from its CEO Jensen Huang on opportunities in “physical AI.” Samsung also benefited from an 11th-hour labor-dispute resolution that averted a crippling 18-day strike.

困境重重

英国与日本当前似乎面临诸多共同难题。这两个伟大的岛国均遭债券市场围困，面临丧失财政信誉的风险。

表象之下，日本拥有更多利好因素，对投资者而言亦是如此。

先从相似之处说起。本就捉襟见肘的财政预算，因政治因素及霍尔木兹海峡引发的全球能源危机而进一步承压。两国国债与货币均面临压力。

自伊朗战争爆发以来，英国10年期国债收益率从4.25%跃升至5.04%，日本则从2.12%升至2.78%。本周日本30年期国债收益率触及4.13%，创1999年该期限国债发行以来最高水平。

在此背景下，日本的致命弱点在于其对海外石油与天然气的依赖。根据国际能源署数据，2024年日本能源总供应量的87%依赖进口，而英国这一比例为48%。

目前，首相高市早苗似乎决心通过补贴维持燃油低价，以减轻民众压力。上周，高市要求政府为燃油补贴编制补充预算，而她此前曾坚称此举并无必要。

根据凯投宏观的估算，在最悲观情景下，若东京方面在油价升至每桶130美元时仍维持补贴，相关支出可能高达GDP的2%。

但与英国相比，日本亦具备深厚优势。首先是政治稳定性。债券投资者最担忧的，似乎是中左翼工党首相基尔·斯塔默将被更挥霍无度的左翼工党领袖取代。

更糟的是，右翼民粹主义政党改革党最终可能上台执政，带来不可预测的后果。相比之下，日本的高市早苗仍广受欢迎，其自民党的执政地位或许比以往任何时候都更加稳固。

更为重要的是日本经济与企业部门的潜在实力。日本在全球人工智能硬件供应链中占据关键——且相较于台湾与韩国而言常被低估——的角色。

这包括半导体设备制造商东京电子与存储芯片制造商铠侠控股等世界领先企业。日本还拥有陶瓷及其他先进材料等细分领域的专业供应商。

这有助于解释为何尽管债市动荡，日本东证指数今年迄今仍上涨11%，而英国富时100指数仅上涨4%。科技股权重更高的日经225指数已上涨19%，甚至跑赢纳斯达克指数12%的涨幅。

因此，英国投资者最大的期望，或许是政府能在不陷入政治或财政崩溃的情况下勉力维持。相比之下，日本提供了所有投资者都渴望的东西：上行潜力。

articles.title: Daily Insights: It still pays to switch jobs, just not as much

paragraphs.en:
It still pays to switch jobs, just not as much




Daily Insights | 21 May 2026




 

The job switching pay premium is at the lowest point in the past seven years

Median after-tax wage growth for those who stayed with their employer versus those who changed employers (Q1 of every year, YoY%)







Source: Bank of America internal data

BANK OF AMERICA INSTITUTE

Bank of America Institute finds job switching ticked up in Q1 2026 compared to the first quarter of last year: the share of employees switching jobs rose to 13.5% in Q1 2026, up from 12.9% in Q1 2025. However, the rate of switching still remains below pre-pandemic and “Great Resignation” levels.

And while it still pays to change jobs, the after-tax wage bump is fading. The pay premium for job switchers is now the lowest since the pandemic. During the “Great Resignation” period in 2022, job switchers saw an 18% year-over-year (YoY) increase in after-tax wages, compared to 7% for job stayers. In Q1 2026, job switchers saw a smaller 8% YoY bump in pay, while job stayers saw a 5% YoY increase.

Our newest publication is out now: Should I stay or should I go? The pay tradeoff.

paragraphs.zh:
跳槽仍能带来薪资增长，但增幅已不如从前

每日洞察 | 2026年5月21日

跳槽薪资溢价降至过去七年最低点

留任者与跳槽者的税后工资中位数增长对比（每年第一季度，同比百分比）

来源：美国银行内部数据

美国银行研究所

美国银行研究所发现，2026年第一季度跳槽比例较去年同期有所上升：跳槽员工占比从2025年第一季度的12.9%升至2026年第一季度的13.5%。然而，跳槽率仍低于疫情前及"大辞职潮"时期的水平。

尽管跳槽仍能带来薪资增长，但税后工资涨幅正在收窄。当前跳槽者的薪资溢价为疫情以来最低。在2022年"大辞职潮"期间，跳槽者税后工资同比增长18%，而留任者增幅为7%。2026年第一季度，跳槽者税后工资同比增幅降至8%，留任者则为5%。

我们的最新报告现已发布：《去还是留？薪资权衡》。

sections.en:
It still pays to switch jobs, just not as much




Daily Insights | 21 May 2026




 

The job switching pay premium is at the lowest point in the past seven years

Median after-tax wage growth for those who stayed with their employer versus those who changed employers (Q1 of every year, YoY%)







Source: Bank of America internal data

BANK OF AMERICA INSTITUTE

Bank of America Institute finds job switching ticked up in Q1 2026 compared to the first quarter of last year: the share of employees switching jobs rose to 13.5% in Q1 2026, up from 12.9% in Q1 2025. However, the rate of switching still remains below pre-pandemic and “Great Resignation” levels.

And while it still pays to change jobs, the after-tax wage bump is fading. The pay premium for job switchers is now the lowest since the pandemic. During the “Great Resignation” period in 2022, job switchers saw an 18% year-over-year (YoY) increase in after-tax wages, compared to 7% for job stayers. In Q1 2026, job switchers saw a smaller 8% YoY bump in pay, while job stayers saw a 5% YoY increase.

Our newest publication is out now: Should I stay or should I go? The pay tradeoff.

留任者与跳槽者的税后工资中位数增长对比（每年第一季度，同比百分比）

来源：美国银行内部数据

美国银行研究所

美国银行研究所发现，2026年第一季度跳槽比例较去年同期有所上升：跳槽员工占比从2025年第一季度的12.9%升至2026年第一季度的13.5%。然而，跳槽率仍低于疫情前及"大辞职潮"时期的水平。

尽管跳槽仍能带来薪资增长，但税后工资涨幅正在收窄。当前跳槽者的薪资溢价为疫情以来最低。在2022年"大辞职潮"期间，跳槽者税后工资同比增长18%，而留任者增幅为7%。2026年第一季度，跳槽者税后工资同比增幅降至8%，留任者则为5%。

我们的最新报告现已发布：《去还是留？薪资权衡》。

paragraphs.en: From the Trading Floor: Why Rates Could Keep Rising
paragraphs.zh: 交易台观点：利率为何可能持续上行

paragraphs.en:
US government bond yields have surged this month. Hotter-than-expected inflation data may be the primary cause, but there are several drivers behind the move, says Phillip Lee, head of Real Money Rate Sales in Goldman Sachs Global Banking & Markets.


US bond yields have surged as sticky inflation, resilient growth, and global yield spillovers push investors to scale back expectations for Federal Reserve cuts and price in pauses and higher rates for longer. At the same time, persistent fiscal deficits, heavy Treasury supply, and rising debt sustainability concerns are driving investors to demand extra compensation to own long-term government debt.


While shorter-term rates have risen as well, the move has been particularly notable in long-term Treasuries. This week, the 30-year yield hit its highest level in 19 years.
paragraphs.zh:
美国国债收益率本月大幅攀升。高盛全球银行与市场部实际利率销售主管菲利普·李表示，高于预期的通胀数据可能是主因，但这一走势背后存在多重驱动因素。

粘性通胀、经济韧性及全球收益率溢出效应，正推动投资者下调对美联储降息的预期，转而押注暂停加息及更长时间维持高利率，导致美国国债收益率上行。与此同时，持续财政赤字、国债供给压力及不断加剧的债务可持续性担忧，正促使投资者要求持有长期国债获得额外补偿。

尽管短期利率同样走高，但长期美债的波动尤为显著。本周，30年期国债收益率触及19年来最高水平。

paragraphs.en:
Lee expects to see the move continue.


“I think rates are going higher,” he says. In particular, he expects that longer-term yields will continue to rise, as investors continue to demand more compensation for owning longer-term bonds, due to the potential for higher inflation and higher bond issuance. Shorter-term rates, on the other hand, could be driven more by Fed policy, which Lee expects to be relatively balanced between hikes and cuts in the years ahead.
paragraphs.zh:
李预计这一趋势将持续。

“我认为利率还会走高，”他表示。他特别指出，长期收益率将继续上升，因为投资者持续要求持有长期债券获得更高补偿，这源于通胀可能上升以及债券发行量增加。另一方面，短期利率可能更多受美联储政策驱动，李预计未来几年美联储的加息与降息将相对平衡。

paragraphs.en: Can Asia’s Stock Rally Continue?
paragraphs.zh: 亚洲股市涨势能否持续？

paragraphs.en:
Asian stocks appear to be on two very different paths, with North Asian markets, such as South Korea, Taiwan, and Japan, pulling ahead of South Asian equities on the strength of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade and their greater insulation from the energy shock. Goldman Sachs Research's Tim Moe outlines the factors driving North Asia's outperformance on the latest episode of Goldman Sachs Exchanges.
The AI memory super cycle is boosting South Korean shares: Moe believes the semiconductor memory boom will last three to five years, far longer than the market is pricing in. With token demand projected to grow 24x by 2030 as uptake of agentic AI grows, supply constraints should sustain pricing power, he says.
China's A-shares outperform: A-shares, which are listed in mainland China and traded in renminbi, are up nearly 10% year to date, bolstered in part by policy support and strong earnings. In contrast, the MSCI China index, a measure of offshore equity performance, is down 2% so far this year, weighed down by softer earnings from the index’s internet-heavy composition. “The story here is better-than-expected earnings delivery for onshore and subpar earnings delivery for offshore,” Moe says.
Japan's bull case remains intact: Political stability following Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's election, solid earnings growth amplified by favorable exchange rates, a normalization of interest rates, and corporate governance reforms are among the factors that make Japan attractive to investors, according to Moe.
Read more about Moe’s prediction for South Korea’s stock market amid surging semiconductor earnings.
paragraphs.zh:
亚洲股市呈现明显分化态势，以韩国、中国台湾和日本为代表的北亚市场凭借人工智能交易优势及对能源冲击更强的抵御能力，正领跑南亚股市。高盛研究部首席策略师Tim Moe在最新一期《高盛交易所》播客中剖析了推动北亚市场表现领先的关键因素。

AI存储超级周期正助推韩国股市：Moe认为半导体存储繁荣将持续三至五年，远超当前市场定价预期。他指出，随着代理型AI应用普及推动代币需求预计在2030年前增长24倍，供应端约束将维持定价能力。

中国A股表现突出：在岸人民币计价的A股年初至今涨幅近10%，政策支持与强劲盈利构成主要支撑。相比之下，衡量离岸股市表现的MSCI中国指数年内下跌2%，主要受互联网板块权重过高导致盈利疲软拖累。Moe表示："核心差异在于在岸市场盈利超预期，而离岸市场盈利不及预期。"

日本牛市逻辑依然成立：Moe认为，首相高市早苗当选后政局稳定、汇率优势放大盈利增长、利率正常化进程及公司治理改革等因素，共同构成日本市场对投资者的吸引力。

更多关于半导体盈利飙升背景下Moe对韩国股市的预测，请参阅相关报道。

paragraphs.en: The Key Number: €45,800,000,000
paragraphs.zh: 关键数字：458亿欧元

paragraphs.en:
German federal spending in April came in at €45.8 billion ($53.3 billion), above our economists’ forecast of €42.2 billion and an increase of €8 billion relative to April 2025.


Germany relaxed its constitutional debt rule last year to allow for higher defense and infrastructure spending. Defense spending so far in 2026 is up 34% from 2025, according to Goldman Sachs Research economist Niklas Garnadt.


While spending in the main budget and the military fund were in line with our economists’ expectations in April, the €6.1 billion of implied spending in the government’s infrastructure and climate fund “exceeded expectations notably,” Garnadt writes in a report.


At the same time, government revenues fell slightly short of expectations. This, along with higher-than-expected spending, resulted in a higher fiscal deficit than our economists anticipated. The cumulative fiscal deficit in the main budget and the two main off-budget funds this year, which now stands at €63.6 billion, is more than twice as wide as in April last year.


Read the full report on rising German federal spending in April.
paragraphs.zh:
德国联邦政府4月支出为458亿欧元（合533亿美元），高于我们经济学家的预测值422亿欧元，较2025年4月增加80亿欧元。

德国去年放宽了宪法规定的债务上限，以允许增加国防和基础设施支出。高盛研究部经济学家Niklas Garnadt指出，2026年迄今的国防支出较2025年增长34%。

Garnadt在报告中写道，尽管4月主要预算和军事基金的支出符合我们经济学家的预期，但政府基础设施与气候基金中隐含的61亿欧元支出"显著超出预期"。

与此同时，政府收入略低于预期。这一情况叠加高于预期的支出，导致财政赤字高于我们经济学家的预测。今年主要预算及两大主要预算外基金的累计财政赤字已达636亿欧元，是去年4月的两倍以上。

阅读关于4月德国联邦支出上升的完整报告。

paragraphs.en:
Access to capital is becoming a focus for water infrastructure as countries facing geopolitical competition, rising demand, and changing weather patterns try to protect their water supply, according to a report from the Goldman Sachs Global Institute and the Sustainable Finance Group.


The World Economic Forum estimates that the global need for investment in water infrastructure through 2040 is €11.4 trillion—€6.5 trillion more than current investment levels.


In response, technological advancements and innovative financing solutions are springing up to direct capital towards water infrastructure and technology, the report says.
Public-private partnerships are a key funding vehicle for governments undertaking infrastructure projects. Governments can de-risk projects through guarantees and anchor investments, helping to “crowd in” private capital. And targeted incentives, including grants, low-interest loans, and regulatory frameworks, can bring promising pilot programs to scale.
Market reforms and rising demand are increasing the opportunity for key technologies, from desalination to enhanced leak monitoring and circular solutions, to better recover costs and to scale up.
Financial innovation can support capital inflows and technological deployment. For example, microfinance provides another route to investing in water markets, and tokenized financing can deliver credits for companies that conserve or recycle water.


Also read an article from Goldman Sachs Asset Management on where investors are finding opportunities in the global response to water stress.
paragraphs.zh:
高盛全球研究所与可持续金融集团联合发布的报告指出，随着各国面临地缘政治竞争、需求增长及气候模式变化，并试图保障自身水资源供应，获取资本正成为水务基础设施领域的焦点议题。

世界经济论坛估计，截至2040年全球水务基础设施投资需求达11.4万亿欧元，较当前投资水平高出6.5万亿欧元。

报告称，为应对这一需求，技术创新与新型融资方案正不断涌现，引导资本流向水务基础设施及相关技术领域。

公私合作伙伴关系是政府开展基础设施项目的重要融资工具。政府可通过担保和锚定投资降低项目风险，从而"撬动"私人资本。同时，包括拨款、低息贷款及监管框架在内的定向激励措施，能够推动有前景的试点项目实现规模化。

市场改革与需求增长正为关键技术的成本回收与规模化发展创造机遇，涵盖海水淡化、增强型泄漏监测及循环解决方案等领域。

金融创新可支撑资本流入与技术部署。例如，小额信贷为投资水务市场提供了新路径，而代币化融资则能为实施节水或水循环利用的企业提供信用额度。

另请参阅高盛资产管理公司关于投资者在全球应对水资源压力中如何寻找机遇的文章。

B) Analyzing, translating, or summarizing documents

A) 撰写或编辑书面通讯
B) 分析、翻译或总结文档

sections.en: From the Trading Floor: Why Rates Could Keep Rising
sections.zh: 交易台观点：利率为何可能持续上行

sections.en:
US government bond yields have surged this month. Hotter-than-expected inflation data may be the primary cause, but there are several drivers behind the move, says Phillip Lee, head of Real Money Rate Sales in Goldman Sachs Global Banking & Markets.


US bond yields have surged as sticky inflation, resilient growth, and global yield spillovers push investors to scale back expectations for Federal Reserve cuts and price in pauses and higher rates for longer. At the same time, persistent fiscal deficits, heavy Treasury supply, and rising debt sustainability concerns are driving investors to demand extra compensation to own long-term government debt.


While shorter-term rates have risen as well, the move has been particularly notable in long-term Treasuries. This week, the 30-year yield hit its highest level in 19 years.
sections.zh:
美国国债收益率本月大幅攀升。高盛全球银行与市场部实际利率销售主管菲利普·李表示，高于预期的通胀数据可能是主因，但这一走势背后存在多重驱动因素。

粘性通胀、经济韧性及全球收益率溢出效应，正推动投资者下调对美联储降息的预期，转而押注暂停加息及更长时间维持高利率，导致美国国债收益率上行。与此同时，持续财政赤字、国债供给压力及不断加剧的债务可持续性担忧，正促使投资者要求持有长期国债获得额外补偿。

尽管短期利率同样走高，但长期美债的波动尤为显著。本周，30年期国债收益率触及19年来最高水平。

sections.en:
Lee expects to see the move continue.


“I think rates are going higher,” he says. In particular, he expects that longer-term yields will continue to rise, as investors continue to demand more compensation for owning longer-term bonds, due to the potential for higher inflation and higher bond issuance. Shorter-term rates, on the other hand, could be driven more by Fed policy, which Lee expects to be relatively balanced between hikes and cuts in the years ahead.
sections.zh:
李预计这一趋势将持续。

“我认为利率还会走高，”他表示。他特别指出，长期收益率将继续上升，因为投资者持续要求持有长期债券获得更高补偿，这源于通胀可能上升以及债券发行量增加。另一方面，短期利率可能更多受美联储政策驱动，李预计未来几年美联储的加息与降息将相对平衡。

sections.en: Can Asia’s Stock Rally Continue?
sections.zh: 亚洲股市涨势能否持续？

sections.en:
Asian stocks appear to be on two very different paths, with North Asian markets, such as South Korea, Taiwan, and Japan, pulling ahead of South Asian equities on the strength of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade and their greater insulation from the energy shock. Goldman Sachs Research's Tim Moe outlines the factors driving North Asia's outperformance on the latest episode of Goldman Sachs Exchanges.
The AI memory super cycle is boosting South Korean shares: Moe believes the semiconductor memory boom will last three to five years, far longer than the market is pricing in. With token demand projected to grow 24x by 2030 as uptake of agentic AI grows, supply constraints should sustain pricing power, he says.
China's A-shares outperform: A-shares, which are listed in mainland China and traded in renminbi, are up nearly 10% year to date, bolstered in part by policy support and strong earnings. In contrast, the MSCI China index, a measure of offshore equity performance, is down 2% so far this year, weighed down by softer earnings from the index’s internet-heavy composition. “The story here is better-than-expected earnings delivery for onshore and subpar earnings delivery for offshore,” Moe says.
Japan's bull case remains intact: Political stability following Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's election, solid earnings growth amplified by favorable exchange rates, a normalization of interest rates, and corporate governance reforms are among the factors that make Japan attractive to investors, according to Moe.
Read more about Moe’s prediction for South Korea’s stock market amid surging semiconductor earnings.
sections.zh:
亚洲股市呈现明显分化态势，以韩国、中国台湾和日本为代表的北亚市场凭借人工智能交易优势及对能源冲击更强的抵御能力，正领跑南亚股市。高盛研究部首席策略师Tim Moe在最新一期《高盛交易所》播客中剖析了推动北亚市场表现领先的关键因素。

AI存储超级周期正助推韩国股市：Moe认为半导体存储繁荣将持续三至五年，远超当前市场定价预期。他指出，随着代理型AI应用普及推动代币需求预计在2030年前增长24倍，供应端约束将维持定价能力。

中国A股表现突出：在岸人民币计价的A股年初至今涨幅近10%，政策支持与强劲盈利构成主要支撑。相比之下，衡量离岸股市表现的MSCI中国指数年内下跌2%，主要受互联网板块权重过高导致盈利疲软拖累。Moe表示："核心差异在于在岸市场盈利超预期，而离岸市场盈利不及预期。"

日本牛市逻辑依然成立：Moe认为，首相高市早苗当选后政局稳定、汇率优势放大盈利增长、利率正常化进程及公司治理改革等因素，共同构成日本市场对投资者的吸引力。

更多关于半导体盈利飙升背景下Moe对韩国股市的预测，请参阅相关报道。

sections.en: The Key Number: €45,800,000,000
sections.zh: 关键数字：458亿欧元

sections.en:
German federal spending in April came in at €45.8 billion ($53.3 billion), above our economists’ forecast of €42.2 billion and an increase of €8 billion relative to April 2025.


Germany relaxed its constitutional debt rule last year to allow for higher defense and infrastructure spending. Defense spending so far in 2026 is up 34% from 2025, according to Goldman Sachs Research economist Niklas Garnadt.


While spending in the main budget and the military fund were in line with our economists’ expectations in April, the €6.1 billion of implied spending in the government’s infrastructure and climate fund “exceeded expectations notably,” Garnadt writes in a report.


At the same time, government revenues fell slightly short of expectations. This, along with higher-than-expected spending, resulted in a higher fiscal deficit than our economists anticipated. The cumulative fiscal deficit in the main budget and the two main off-budget funds this year, which now stands at €63.6 billion, is more than twice as wide as in April last year.


Read the full report on rising German federal spending in April.
sections.zh:
德国联邦政府4月支出为458亿欧元（合533亿美元），高于我们经济学家的预测值422亿欧元，较2025年4月增加80亿欧元。

德国去年放宽了宪法规定的债务上限，以允许增加国防和基础设施支出。高盛研究部经济学家Niklas Garnadt指出，2026年迄今的国防支出较2025年增长34%。

Garnadt在报告中写道，尽管4月主要预算和军事基金的支出符合我们经济学家的预期，但政府基础设施与气候基金中隐含的61亿欧元支出"显著超出预期"。

与此同时，政府收入略低于预期。这一情况叠加高于预期的支出，导致财政赤字高于我们经济学家的预测。今年主要预算及两大主要预算外基金的累计财政赤字已达636亿欧元，是去年4月的两倍以上。

阅读关于4月德国联邦支出上升的完整报告。

sections.en:
Access to capital is becoming a focus for water infrastructure as countries facing geopolitical competition, rising demand, and changing weather patterns try to protect their water supply, according to a report from the Goldman Sachs Global Institute and the Sustainable Finance Group.


The World Economic Forum estimates that the global need for investment in water infrastructure through 2040 is €11.4 trillion—€6.5 trillion more than current investment levels.


In response, technological advancements and innovative financing solutions are springing up to direct capital towards water infrastructure and technology, the report says.
Public-private partnerships are a key funding vehicle for governments undertaking infrastructure projects. Governments can de-risk projects through guarantees and anchor investments, helping to “crowd in” private capital. And targeted incentives, including grants, low-interest loans, and regulatory frameworks, can bring promising pilot programs to scale.
Market reforms and rising demand are increasing the opportunity for key technologies, from desalination to enhanced leak monitoring and circular solutions, to better recover costs and to scale up.
Financial innovation can support capital inflows and technological deployment. For example, microfinance provides another route to investing in water markets, and tokenized financing can deliver credits for companies that conserve or recycle water.


Also read an article from Goldman Sachs Asset Management on where investors are finding opportunities in the global response to water stress.
sections.zh:
高盛全球研究所与可持续金融集团联合发布的报告指出，随着各国面临地缘政治竞争、需求增长及气候模式变化，并试图保障自身水资源供应，获取资本正成为水务基础设施领域的焦点议题。

世界经济论坛估计，截至2040年全球水务基础设施投资需求达11.4万亿欧元，较当前投资水平高出6.5万亿欧元。

报告称，为应对这一需求，技术创新与新型融资方案正不断涌现，引导资本流向水务基础设施及相关技术领域。

公私合作伙伴关系是政府开展基础设施项目的重要融资工具。政府可通过担保和锚定投资降低项目风险，从而"撬动"私人资本。同时，包括拨款、低息贷款及监管框架在内的定向激励措施，能够推动有前景的试点项目实现规模化。

市场改革与需求增长正为关键技术的成本回收与规模化发展创造机遇，涵盖海水淡化、增强型泄漏监测及循环解决方案等领域。

金融创新可支撑资本流入与技术部署。例如，小额信贷为投资水务市场提供了新路径，而代币化融资则能为实施节水或水循环利用的企业提供信用额度。

另请参阅高盛资产管理公司关于投资者在全球应对水资源压力中如何寻找机遇的文章。

Software stocks sold off at the start of this year amid fears about AI disrupting the business models of software-as-a-service companies.


Among US firms using generative AI, what’s the most commonly cited work task that they use it for, according to Goldman Sachs Research?


A) Writing or editing written communications
B) Analyzing, translating, or summarizing documents
C) Developing or researching new projects
D) Software coding or debugging

今年年初，软件股遭遇抛售，原因是市场担忧人工智能会颠覆软件即服务公司的商业模式。

paragraphs.en: For Retailers, It’s One Battle After Another
paragraphs.zh: 对于零售商而言，这是一场又一场的战役。

paragraphs.en:
Good morning, I’m filling in for Spencer Jakab today. It doesn’t look like markets are ready to shake off Friday’s jitters. Futures point to a moderately down open for stocks, Brent crude oil prices are up a touch and U.S. Treasury yields are holding on after their sharp rise at the end of last week. Skirmishing over the weekend in the Gulf and on Truth Social is reminding investors that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and that there is little sign of a near-term reopening.



 



​📈 Follow our live markets data and coverage.



 


-	Last	Chg%


↓ S&P 500 FUTURES

	7,402.00	-0.41%


↓ DJIA FUTURES

	49,276.00	-0.69%


↓ NASDAQ 100 FUTURES

	29,138.25	-0.32%


↑ U.S. 10 YEAR TREASURY NOTE

	4.61	+0.24


↑ CRUDE OIL

	106.29	+0.83%


 


5/18/2026, 6:29:20 AM ET


 


 


 


Gas versus refunds


 



In recent years, retailers have faced endless supply-chain challenges. Now comes the Iran war.  



 



Retailers are starting to report results for their fiscal first quarter, which spans February through April. That means it included two full months of the conflict. The disruption will be a test early into the tenures of the newly minted CEOs at Walmart and Target, both of which report this week. 



 



Both executives are longtime employees who have taken the helm at pivotal moments. Target is in the middle of a turnaround effort; Walmart is proving out tech-like growth. Investors like the stories. Target and Walmart shares are up 24% and 18% this year, respectively, outpacing the market. 



 



Gas prices could get in the way, though. Walmart executives, speaking at a Citi sector conference in March, said gas prices close to $4 a gallon cause consumers to trade down to cheaper options. Prices at $5 a gallon become more of a shock, according to a note from the bank. 



 



Nationwide retail gas prices have hovered close to $4 a gallon since April and have been closer to $4.50 since May.



 



But there is a counterweight. Tax-refund season was particularly generous because of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Americans in aggregate received 18% more in refunds than they did a year earlier, according to Steven Shemesh, equity analyst at RBC Capital Markets. This translates to roughly $50 billion of additional dollars circulating in the economy.



 



In other words, retailers’ top lines for the quarter aren’t likely to show much damage from the Iran conflict. 



 



The bottom line might be different. In aggregate, retailers in the S&P 500 have expanded margins over the past few years, even during stretches of high inflation. Last year, the group’s operating margins were at their highest levels since S&P Global Market Intelligence started tracking the data in 2006.



 



Now, prices are rising for everything from fertilizer, plastics, aluminum and fuel, potentially squeezing margins. 



 



For Walmart, the bottom line matters because its tech-like growth story, which has helped catapult its share price to 43 times forward earnings, is predicated on growing operating profits faster than revenue. Much of this is thanks to high-margin revenue sources such as advertising and membership fees.



 



Rising costs could undermine that growth. Last week, Walmart said it would cut or relocate about 1,000 corporate workers. 



 



Retail giants like Walmart, Target and Costco, which reports later in the month, are better positioned than most in a rising price environment. They tend to have bargaining power with suppliers, sell necessities and are seen as value destinations. Target’s decision to invest in groceries seems prescient. 



 



Still, the longer the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, the harder it will be for retailers to hold the line on margins.



 





 




 


 



This is an edition of the Markets A.M. newsletter, preparing you for the trading day ahead with expert insight into the companies and industries set to move markets. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.



 


 


 


Stocks I’m Watching


 



↗️ Dominion Energy: The utility company is in talks to be acquired by NextEra Energy in what would be one of the largest deals of the year. Dominion shares climbed 12% premarket, while NextEra’s edged lower. The deal could come as soon as today, The Wall Street Journal reported.



 



↘️UnitedHealth Group: The health insurer’s stock dropped 5% premarket after Berkshire Hathaway disclosed late on Friday it eliminated its stake in the company. Berkshire also said it bought shares of Delta and Macy’s last quarter, helping propel the companies’ stocks higher before the bell.



 



↘️Regeneron: Shares of the biotech company slid more than 10% premarket after it said late on Friday that a late-stage clinical trial for a melanoma treatment failed to meet its goals.



 



↘️ Ryanair: The Irish budget airline’s stock fell more than 3% after it warned the war in the Middle East is driving up fuel costs and weighing on fares as customers delay booking trips.

2026年5月18日，美国东部时间上午6:29:20

汽油价格与退税

近年来，零售商面临了无尽的供应链挑战。如今，伊朗战争又接踵而至。

零售商正陆续公布涵盖2月至4月的第一财季业绩。这意味着该季度包含了冲突爆发后的整整两个月。这场干扰将考验沃尔玛和塔吉特新任CEO的早期任期，这两家公司均于本周发布财报。

两位高管均为长期任职的员工，在关键时刻接掌帅印。塔吉特正处于转型努力之中；沃尔玛则正在证明其科技型增长模式。投资者看好这些故事。塔吉特和沃尔玛的股价今年分别上涨了24%和18%，跑赢大盘。

然而，汽油价格可能成为阻碍。沃尔玛高管在3月份的花旗行业会议上表示，当汽油价格接近每加仑4美元时，消费者会转向更便宜的选择。该银行的一份报告指出，每加仑5美元的价格则会造成更大的冲击。

自4月以来，全美零售汽油价格一直徘徊在每加仑4美元附近，自5月以来更接近4.50美元。

但有一个抵消因素。由于《一项大而美的法案》，退税季格外慷慨。根据加拿大皇家银行资本市场股票分析师史蒂文·谢梅什的数据，美国民众获得的退税总额比去年同期增长了18%。这意味着约有500亿美元的额外资金在经济中流通。

换句话说，零售商本季度的营收可能不会显示出伊朗冲突造成的太大损害。

但利润情况可能有所不同。总体而言，标普500指数中的零售商在过去几年中，即使在通胀高企时期，也扩大了利润率。去年，该群体的营业利润率达到了自标普全球市场财智2006年开始追踪该数据以来的最高水平。

如今，从化肥、塑料、铝到燃料，各类价格都在上涨，这可能会挤压利润率。

对沃尔玛而言，利润至关重要，因为其科技型增长故事——该故事已将其股价推高至43倍远期市盈率——建立在营业利润增速快于营收的基础之上。这很大程度上归功于广告和会员费等利润率较高的收入来源。

成本上升可能削弱这一增长。上周，沃尔玛表示将裁减或调动约1000名企业员工。

像沃尔玛、塔吉特和好市多（后者将于本月晚些时候公布财报）这样的零售巨头，在价格上涨的环境下比大多数公司更具优势。它们通常对供应商有议价能力，销售必需品，并被视为物美价廉的目的地。塔吉特投资杂货业务的决定似乎颇有先见之明。

尽管如此，霍尔木兹海峡关闭的时间越长，零售商就越难守住利润率底线。

Gas versus refunds


 



In recent years, retailers have faced endless supply-chain challenges. Now comes the Iran war.  



 



Retailers are starting to report results for their fiscal first quarter, which spans February through April. That means it included two full months of the conflict. The disruption will be a test early into the tenures of the newly minted CEOs at Walmart and Target, both of which report this week. 



 



Both executives are longtime employees who have taken the helm at pivotal moments. Target is in the middle of a turnaround effort; Walmart is proving out tech-like growth. Investors like the stories. Target and Walmart shares are up 24% and 18% this year, respectively, outpacing the market. 



 



Gas prices could get in the way, though. Walmart executives, speaking at a Citi sector conference in March, said gas prices close to $4 a gallon cause consumers to trade down to cheaper options. Prices at $5 a gallon become more of a shock, according to a note from the bank. 



 



Nationwide retail gas prices have hovered close to $4 a gallon since April and have been closer to $4.50 since May.



 



But there is a counterweight. Tax-refund season was particularly generous because of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Americans in aggregate received 18% more in refunds than they did a year earlier, according to Steven Shemesh, equity analyst at RBC Capital Markets. This translates to roughly $50 billion of additional dollars circulating in the economy.



 



In other words, retailers’ top lines for the quarter aren’t likely to show much damage from the Iran conflict. 



 



The bottom line might be different. In aggregate, retailers in the S&P 500 have expanded margins over the past few years, even during stretches of high inflation. Last year, the group’s operating margins were at their highest levels since S&P Global Market Intelligence started tracking the data in 2006.



 



Now, prices are rising for everything from fertilizer, plastics, aluminum and fuel, potentially squeezing margins. 



 



For Walmart, the bottom line matters because its tech-like growth story, which has helped catapult its share price to 43 times forward earnings, is predicated on growing operating profits faster than revenue. Much of this is thanks to high-margin revenue sources such as advertising and membership fees.



 



Rising costs could undermine that growth. Last week, Walmart said it would cut or relocate about 1,000 corporate workers. 



 



Retail giants like Walmart, Target and Costco, which reports later in the month, are better positioned than most in a rising price environment. They tend to have bargaining power with suppliers, sell necessities and are seen as value destinations. Target’s decision to invest in groceries seems prescient. 



 



Still, the longer the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, the harder it will be for retailers to hold the line on margins.



 





 




 


 



This is an edition of the Markets A.M. newsletter, preparing you for the trading day ahead with expert insight into the companies and industries set to move markets. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.



 


 


 


Stocks I’m Watching


 



↗️ Dominion Energy: The utility company is in talks to be acquired by NextEra Energy in what would be one of the largest deals of the year. Dominion shares climbed 12% premarket, while NextEra’s edged lower. The deal could come as soon as today, The Wall Street Journal reported.



 



↘️UnitedHealth Group: The health insurer’s stock dropped 5% premarket after Berkshire Hathaway disclosed late on Friday it eliminated its stake in the company. Berkshire also said it bought shares of Delta and Macy’s last quarter, helping propel the companies’ stocks higher before the bell.



 



↘️Regeneron: Shares of the biotech company slid more than 10% premarket after it said late on Friday that a late-stage clinical trial for a melanoma treatment failed to meet its goals.



 



↘️ Ryanair: The Irish budget airline’s stock fell more than 3% after it warned the war in the Middle East is driving up fuel costs and weighing on fares as customers delay booking trips.

汽油价格与退税

近年来，零售商面临了无尽的供应链挑战。如今，伊朗战争又接踵而至。

零售商正陆续公布涵盖2月至4月的第一财季业绩。这意味着该季度包含了冲突爆发后的整整两个月。这场干扰将考验沃尔玛和塔吉特新任CEO的早期任期，这两家公司均于本周发布财报。

两位高管均为长期任职的员工，在关键时刻接掌帅印。塔吉特正处于转型努力之中；沃尔玛则正在证明其科技型增长模式。投资者看好这些故事。塔吉特和沃尔玛的股价今年分别上涨了24%和18%，跑赢大盘。

然而，汽油价格可能成为阻碍。沃尔玛高管在3月份的花旗行业会议上表示，当汽油价格接近每加仑4美元时，消费者会转向更便宜的选择。该银行的一份报告指出，每加仑5美元的价格则会造成更大的冲击。

自4月以来，全美零售汽油价格一直徘徊在每加仑4美元附近，自5月以来更接近4.50美元。

但有一个抵消因素。由于《一项大而美的法案》，退税季格外慷慨。根据加拿大皇家银行资本市场股票分析师史蒂文·谢梅什的数据，美国民众获得的退税总额比去年同期增长了18%。这意味着约有500亿美元的额外资金在经济中流通。

换句话说，零售商本季度的营收可能不会显示出伊朗冲突造成的太大损害。

但利润情况可能有所不同。总体而言，标普500指数中的零售商在过去几年中，即使在通胀高企时期，也扩大了利润率。去年，该群体的营业利润率达到了自标普全球市场财智2006年开始追踪该数据以来的最高水平。

如今，从化肥、塑料、铝到燃料，各类价格都在上涨，这可能会挤压利润率。

对沃尔玛而言，利润至关重要，因为其科技型增长故事——该故事已将其股价推高至43倍远期市盈率——建立在营业利润增速快于营收的基础之上。这很大程度上归功于广告和会员费等利润率较高的收入来源。

成本上升可能削弱这一增长。上周，沃尔玛表示将裁减或调动约1000名企业员工。

像沃尔玛、塔吉特和好市多（后者将于本月晚些时候公布财报）这样的零售巨头，在价格上涨的环境下比大多数公司更具优势。它们通常对供应商有议价能力，销售必需品，并被视为物美价廉的目的地。塔吉特投资杂货业务的决定似乎颇有先见之明。

尽管如此，霍尔木兹海峡关闭的时间越长，零售商就越难守住利润率底线。

articles.title: Tomorrow and Tomorrow

paragraphs.en:
What Happened in Markets Today



Tech stocks fell as investors rotated out of AI-focused stocks.  Nvidia, which reports earnings on Wednesday, fell 1.3% and the Nasdaq declined 0.5%. The S&P 500, which has become increasingly exposed to tech stocks, fell less than 0.1%. The Dow Jones Industrials advanced 0.3%.

Investors remain concerned that the disruption to energy markets poses a threat to the global economy. Futures tied to Brent crude, the global crude benchmark, have floated up to about $112 a barrel. Treasury yields stabilized after closing at their highest level in more than a year on Friday. President Trump posted a message on social media late Monday saying he had postponed strikes on Iran that had been planned for tomorrow, citing progress in talks.

Dominion Energy has agreed to be acquired by NextEra Energy in what would be one of the largest deals of the year. Dominion shares were up 9.4% while NextEra's were down 4.6%.  

UnitedHealth Group's stock dropped 0.7% after Berkshire Hathaway disclosed late on Friday that it had eliminated its stake in the company. Berkshire also said it bought shares of Delta and Macy's last quarter. Delta and Macy's were each up less than 1%.

President Trump will host a swearing-in ceremony for incoming Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh at the White House on Friday. The last new Fed chair sworn in at the White House was Alan Greenspan in 1987. More recent ceremonies have been held at the Fed.
paragraphs.zh:
今日市场动态

科技股下跌，投资者正从人工智能概念股中撤资。将于周三公布财报的英伟达下跌1.3%，纳斯达克指数下跌0.5%。对科技股敞口日益扩大的标普500指数跌幅不足0.1%。道琼斯工业指数上涨0.3%。

投资者仍担忧能源市场动荡对全球经济构成威胁。作为全球原油基准的布伦特原油期货价格已升至约每桶112美元。美国国债收益率在上周五收于一年多来最高水平后趋于稳定。特朗普总统周一晚间在社交媒体发文称，鉴于谈判取得进展，他已推迟原定于明日对伊朗实施的打击。

多米尼恩能源公司同意被NextEra Energy收购，这将成为年内规模最大的交易之一。多米尼恩股价上涨9.4%，NextEra股价下跌4.6%。

联合健康集团股价下跌0.7%，此前伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司上周五晚间披露已清仓该股。伯克希尔还表示上季度买入了达美航空和梅西百货的股票。达美航空和梅西百货股价均上涨不足1%。

特朗普总统将于周五在白宫为即将上任的美联储主席凯文·沃什主持宣誓就职仪式。上一位在白宫宣誓就职的美联储主席是1987年的艾伦·格林斯潘。近年来的此类仪式均在美联储总部举行。

sections.en:
What Happened in Markets Today



Tech stocks fell as investors rotated out of AI-focused stocks.  Nvidia, which reports earnings on Wednesday, fell 1.3% and the Nasdaq declined 0.5%. The S&P 500, which has become increasingly exposed to tech stocks, fell less than 0.1%. The Dow Jones Industrials advanced 0.3%.

Investors remain concerned that the disruption to energy markets poses a threat to the global economy. Futures tied to Brent crude, the global crude benchmark, have floated up to about $112 a barrel. Treasury yields stabilized after closing at their highest level in more than a year on Friday. President Trump posted a message on social media late Monday saying he had postponed strikes on Iran that had been planned for tomorrow, citing progress in talks.

Dominion Energy has agreed to be acquired by NextEra Energy in what would be one of the largest deals of the year. Dominion shares were up 9.4% while NextEra's were down 4.6%.  

UnitedHealth Group's stock dropped 0.7% after Berkshire Hathaway disclosed late on Friday that it had eliminated its stake in the company. Berkshire also said it bought shares of Delta and Macy's last quarter. Delta and Macy's were each up less than 1%.

President Trump will host a swearing-in ceremony for incoming Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh at the White House on Friday. The last new Fed chair sworn in at the White House was Alan Greenspan in 1987. More recent ceremonies have been held at the Fed.

Brent crude prices are holding at around $110 a barrel, while Treasury yields remain at multiyear highs. With earnings from most of the S&P 500 out of the way, save Nvidia, investors are again focusing on prospects for higher-for-longer-inflation.

5/19/2026, 6:26:48 AM ET


 


 


 


Buyback bellwether


 



One of the stock market’s favorite tailwinds, share buybacks, has been fading for tech titans. Nvidia could be an exception when it reports quarterly results Wednesday.



 



Share repurchases are down sharply for the rest of the Magnificent Seven this year, while buybacks for the S&P 500 overall are holding relatively steady. Excluding Nvidia, the Magnificent Seven’s buybacks last quarter were just under $17 billion. That was 55% lower than the prior quarter and 71% less than a year earlier.



 



Nvidia is the last of the Mag 7 megacaps to report, and investors are eager to see if the chip company has been loading up on its own stock or cutting back.



 



Nvidia spent about $40 billion on buybacks during its last fiscal year, which ended in January. That was up 19% from a year earlier. However, repurchases plummeted to less than $4 billion in the fourth quarter, a two-year low. That was even though Nvidia has free cash flow to spare.



 



Each company’s situation is unique, of course. Amazon.com and Tesla have long eschewed buybacks. But for other big tech companies, the need to spend on AI infrastructure is crowding out other priorities, including keeping shareholders sweet with buybacks. 



 



Apple and Microsoft both lightened up on buybacks in the latest quarter. Meta and Alphabet, once prodigious buyers of their own stock, didn’t repurchase any shares during the first quarter. Meta didn’t buy any during the fourth quarter, either.



 



That is a big departure from their usual practice. Last year, both Meta and Alphabet spent most of their free cash flow on share repurchases. That helped offset dilution from stock-based compensation for employees.



 



While there is broad consensus that buybacks help boost stock prices, nobody really knows how much. “The debate is about the degree,” says James White, chief executive of investment manager Elm Wealth.



 



At the end of last week, more than 90% of S&P 500 companies had filed their latest quarterly results. Repurchases at those companies were about $256 billion, up 12% from a quarter earlier but down 1% from a year earlier, according to data compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence.



 



Nvidia, of course, is a major beneficiary of the rest of the Mag 7’s AI spending, putting it in a different situation. It still had $58.5 billion left in its share-buyback authorization when it last reported. By comparison, the average analyst estimate for Nvidia buybacks this fiscal year is about $55 billion, according to Visible Alpha.



 



In a note last week, UBS analysts said they see potential for a new authorization that could approach $150 billion over the next 12 months. Shareholders no doubt would welcome that. But if Nvidia reports a second consecutive down quarter, it would reinforce the idea that the buybacks tailwind is weakening, not just for big tech but for the market as a whole.

Stocks I’m Watching


 



↗️ ServiceNow: Bank of America analysts said ServiceNow would benefit from AI, and gave the stock a buy rating yesterday, sending it up 8%. The business-software company’s shares are up again premarket; they are still down about a third year to date.



 



↘️ CoreWeave: The stock is down premarket after The Wall Street Journal reported that Alphabet and Blackstone plan to create an artificial-intelligence cloud company to rival CoreWeave using Google’s specialized chips. CoreWeave competitor Nebius is also down premarket. Alphabet and Blackstone shares ticked up ahead of the bell.



 



↘️ SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics: Shares of the two chip companies, which have driven up Korea’s stock market for much of the year, fell, dragging down the Kospi index.



 



↘️ Vallourec: ArcelorMittal said it sold down its stake in Vallourec, a French maker of steel tubes. Shares fell in Paris.

回购风向标

股市最受青睐的顺风因素之一——股票回购，对科技巨头而言正在减弱。英伟达可能是个例外，该公司将于周三公布季度业绩。

今年，除英伟达外，“科技七巨头”其余公司的股票回购大幅下降，而标普500指数整体的回购则相对稳定。剔除英伟达后，“科技七巨头”上季度的回购总额略低于170亿美元，较前一季度下降55%，较去年同期下降71%。

英伟达是“科技七巨头”中最后一家公布财报的巨型公司，投资者迫切想知道这家芯片公司是在大举回购自身股票，还是在削减回购规模。

在截至1月份的上一个财年，英伟达在回购上花费了约400亿美元，同比增长19%。然而，第四季度回购额骤降至不到40亿美元，为两年低点，尽管英伟达拥有充裕的自由现金流。

当然，每家公司的具体情况各不相同。亚马逊和特斯拉长期以来一直回避股票回购。但对于其他大型科技公司而言，在人工智能基础设施上的投入需求正挤占其他优先事项，包括通过回购来取悦股东。

苹果和微软在最近一个季度均减少了回购。Meta和Alphabet曾是自身股票的大买家，但在第一季度未回购任何股票。Meta在第四季度也未进行回购。

这与它们的一贯做法大相径庭。去年，Meta和Alphabet都将大部分自由现金流用于股票回购，这有助于抵消员工股权激励带来的稀释效应。

尽管市场普遍认为回购有助于提振股价，但没人确切知道影响有多大。“争论的焦点在于程度，”投资管理公司Elm Wealth的首席执行官詹姆斯·怀特表示。

截至上周末，超过90%的标普500指数成分股公司已提交最新季度财报。根据标普全球市场情报汇编的数据，这些公司的回购总额约为2560亿美元，较前一季度增长12%，但较去年同期下降1%。

当然，英伟达是“科技七巨头”中其他公司人工智能支出的主要受益者，这使其处于不同境地。在上次公布财报时，其股票回购授权余额仍有585亿美元。相比之下，根据Visible Alpha的数据，分析师对英伟达本财年回购额的平均预估约为550亿美元。

瑞银分析师在上周的一份报告中表示，他们认为未来12个月内英伟达可能推出新的回购授权，规模或接近1500亿美元。股东无疑会对此表示欢迎。但如果英伟达连续第二个季度报告回购下降，将强化这样一种观点：回购这一顺风因素正在减弱，不仅对大型科技股如此，对整个市场亦然。

我关注的股票

↗️ ServiceNow：美国银行分析师表示，ServiceNow将从人工智能中受益，并于昨日给予该股买入评级，推动其上涨8%。这家商业软件公司的股价在盘前交易中再次上涨；但年初至今仍下跌约三分之一。

↘️ CoreWeave：该股盘前下跌，此前《华尔街日报》报道称，Alphabet和黑石集团计划利用谷歌的专用芯片，创建一家人工智能云公司，与CoreWeave竞争。CoreWeave的竞争对手Nebius盘前也出现下跌。Alphabet和黑石集团的股价在开盘前小幅上涨。

↘️ SK海力士、三星电子：这两家芯片公司今年大部分时间推动韩国股市上涨，但其股价今日下跌，拖累韩国综合指数走低。

↘️ Vallourec：安赛乐米塔尔表示已减持其在法国钢管制造商Vallourec的股份。该股在巴黎市场下跌。

我关注的股票

↗️ ServiceNow：美国银行分析师表示，ServiceNow将从人工智能中受益，并于昨日给予该股买入评级，推动其上涨8%。这家商业软件公司的股价在盘前交易中再次上涨；但年初至今仍下跌约三分之一。

↘️ CoreWeave：该股盘前下跌，此前《华尔街日报》报道称，Alphabet和黑石集团计划利用谷歌的专用芯片，创建一家人工智能云公司，与CoreWeave竞争。CoreWeave的竞争对手Nebius盘前也出现下跌。Alphabet和黑石集团的股价在开盘前小幅上涨。

↘️ SK海力士、三星电子：这两家芯片公司今年大部分时间推动韩国股市上涨，但其股价今日下跌，拖累韩国综合指数走低。

↘️ Vallourec：安赛乐米塔尔表示已减持其在法国钢管制造商Vallourec的股份。该股在巴黎市场下跌。

One of the stock market’s favorite tailwinds, share buybacks, has been fading for tech titans. Nvidia could be an exception when it reports quarterly results Wednesday.
sections.zh: 股市最受青睐的利好因素之一——股票回购——对科技巨头而言正在减弱。英伟达周三公布季度业绩时，可能是个例外。

sections.en: Share repurchases are down sharply for the rest of the Magnificent Seven this year, while buybacks for the S&P 500 overall are holding relatively steady. Excluding Nvidia, the Magnificent Seven’s buybacks last quarter were just under $17 billion. That was 55% lower than the prior quarter and 71% less than a year earlier.
sections.zh: 今年，“美股七巨头”中其余六家的股票回购大幅下降，而标普500整体的回购规模则保持相对稳定。剔除英伟达后，“七巨头”上一季度的回购总额略低于170亿美元，较前一季度减少55%，同比下滑71%。

sections.en: Nvidia is the last of the Mag 7 megacaps to report, and investors are eager to see if the chip company has been loading up on its own stock or cutting back.
sections.zh: 英伟达是“美股七巨头”中最后一家发布财报的，投资者迫切想知道这家芯片公司是在增持自家股票还是减持。

sections.en: Nvidia spent about $40 billion on buybacks during its last fiscal year, which ended in January. That was up 19% from a year earlier. However, repurchases plummeted to less than $4 billion in the fourth quarter, a two-year low. That was even though Nvidia has free cash flow to spare.
sections.zh: 英伟达在截至1月的上一财年斥资约400亿美元用于股票回购，同比增长19%。然而，第四季度回购额骤降至不足40亿美元，创两年新低。尽管该公司仍有充裕的自由现金流。

sections.en: Each company’s situation is unique, of course. Amazon.com and Tesla have long eschewed buybacks. But for other big tech companies, the need to spend on AI infrastructure is crowding out other priorities, including keeping shareholders sweet with buybacks.
sections.zh: 当然，每家公司的具体情况各不相同。亚马逊和特斯拉长期回避股票回购。但对于其他大型科技公司而言，在人工智能基础设施上的支出需求正挤占其他优先事项，包括通过股票回购来取悦股东。

articles.recap_en: **Recap:** The article highlights that buybacks among Big Tech are sharply declining—excluding Nvidia, the Magnificent Seven’s repurchases fell 55% quarter-over-quarter and 71% year-over-year to under $17 billion—as AI infrastructure spending crowds out shareholder returns. Nvidia, however, is the potential exception: it still has $58.5 billion in buyback authorization, and UBS sees a possible new $150 billion authorization, making its upcoming earnings a key test for whether the buyback tailwind can persist. If Nvidia reports a second straight down quarter in buybacks, it would reinforce concerns that a major market support is weakening.
articles.recap_zh: 根据华尔街日报报道，大型科技公司的股票回购趋势正在减弱，但英伟达（Nvidia）可能成为例外。数据显示，除英伟达外，“美股七巨头”上季度回购总额仅约170亿美元，环比下降55%，同比下降71%；而英伟达上一财年回购约400亿美元，但第四季度回购骤降至不足40亿美元，创两年新低。市场关注英伟达本周三财报是否会延续回购，若连续两个季度下滑，将强化回购这一市场利好因素正在减弱的信号，对科技股及整体市场情绪构成潜在压力。

articles.title: Daily Insights: Transportation fuels small business payroll growth in April

paragraphs.en:
Transportation fuels small business payroll growth in April




Daily Insights | 19 May 2026




 

Small firms in agriculture, retail, health services and transportation posted payroll growth gains in April

Contribution to overall year-over-year payroll payments per small business client by industry (percentage points, monthly, three-month moving average)







Source: Bank of America internal data

BANK OF AMERICA INSTITUTE

Payroll growth per small business client continued to slow in April, according to Bank of America payments data – a sign the small business labor market is losing some momentum, even if not every industry feels it equally. Small firms in agriculture, retail, healthcare and transportation were positive contributors.

Transportation stood out thanks to strong demand for couriers and messengers, while healthcare has quietly underpinned job creation for more than a year. Still, zooming out, small businesses will likely remain hesitant to hire as operating costs like fuel continue to rise.

Read more in our May Small Business Checkpoint.

运输业推动4月小企业薪资增长

每日洞察 | 2026年5月19日

4月，农业、零售、医疗服务和运输业的小型企业薪资支付实现增长

各行业对小型企业客户整体薪资同比增速的贡献（百分点，月度，三个月移动平均）

来源：美国银行内部数据

美国银行研究所

根据美国银行支付数据，4月小型企业客户人均薪资增速持续放缓——这表明小企业劳动力市场正在失去部分动能，尽管各行业感受不一。农业、零售、医疗保健和运输业的小型企业为正向贡献者。

运输业因快递和信使服务需求强劲而表现突出，而医疗保健行业在过去一年多里一直悄然支撑着就业增长。然而，放眼全局，随着燃油等运营成本持续上升，小企业可能仍将保持谨慎的招聘态度。

articles.title: Spiking Yields

paragraphs.en:
What Happened in Markets Today



U.S. stocks retreated as investors debate tech valuations and worry that a prolonged Iran conflict will keep oil prices rising, pushing up inflation. The S&P 500 fell 0.7%, the Nasdaq dropped 0.8%, and the Dow declined 0.7%.

The global bond selloff is intensifying, putting pressure on government finances and market valuations. Yields on 30-year Treasurys are at 5.18%, their highest level since 2007. Yields on 10-year U.S. Treasury notes rose for a third straight day, hitting their highest closing level since January 2025. 

Oil prices slipped, with Brent crude losing 0.7% to $111.28 a barrel after President Trump said he would hold off on attacking Iran at the request of Gulf leaders. Even so, benchmark Brent crude prices are up more than 20% over the past month.

CoreWeave fell 3.8%. The Wall Street Journal reported that Alphabet and Blackstone plan to create an artificial-intelligence cloud company to rival CoreWeave using Google’s specialized chips. CoreWeave competitor Nebius also slipped 1%.

The number of homes going under contract in the U.S. rose in April, according to a monthly index. The pending home sales index, a leading indicator of house sales based on contract signings, rose 1.4% on month to 74.8. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal had forecast a 1% increase.
paragraphs.zh:
**今日市场动态**

美国股市回落，投资者对科技股估值展开辩论，并担忧伊朗冲突持续将推高油价、加剧通胀。标普500指数下跌0.7%，纳斯达克指数下跌0.8%，道琼斯指数下跌0.7%。

全球债券抛售潮加剧，对政府财政及市场估值构成压力。30年期美国国债收益率升至5.18%，创2007年以来新高。10年期美国国债收益率连续第三日上涨，收于2025年1月以来最高水平。

油价小幅走低，布伦特原油下跌0.7%至每桶111.28美元。此前特朗普总统表示，应海湾国家领导人请求，将暂缓对伊朗发动攻击。即便如此，基准布伦特原油价格过去一个月仍累计上涨逾20%。

CoreWeave股价下跌3.8%。《华尔街日报》报道称，Alphabet与黑石集团计划利用谷歌专用芯片成立一家人工智能云公司，与CoreWeave展开竞争。CoreWeave竞争对手Nebius股价亦下跌1%。

月度指数显示，4月份美国签约购房数量上升。作为基于合同签约量的房屋销售先行指标，成屋签约销售指数环比上升1.4%至74.8。《华尔街日报》调查的经济学家此前预计增幅为1%。

sections.en:
What Happened in Markets Today



U.S. stocks retreated as investors debate tech valuations and worry that a prolonged Iran conflict will keep oil prices rising, pushing up inflation. The S&P 500 fell 0.7%, the Nasdaq dropped 0.8%, and the Dow declined 0.7%.

The global bond selloff is intensifying, putting pressure on government finances and market valuations. Yields on 30-year Treasurys are at 5.18%, their highest level since 2007. Yields on 10-year U.S. Treasury notes rose for a third straight day, hitting their highest closing level since January 2025. 

Oil prices slipped, with Brent crude losing 0.7% to $111.28 a barrel after President Trump said he would hold off on attacking Iran at the request of Gulf leaders. Even so, benchmark Brent crude prices are up more than 20% over the past month.

CoreWeave fell 3.8%. The Wall Street Journal reported that Alphabet and Blackstone plan to create an artificial-intelligence cloud company to rival CoreWeave using Google’s specialized chips. CoreWeave competitor Nebius also slipped 1%.

The number of homes going under contract in the U.S. rose in April, according to a monthly index. The pending home sales index, a leading indicator of house sales based on contract signings, rose 1.4% on month to 74.8. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal had forecast a 1% increase.

全球债券抛售潮加剧，对政府财政及市场估值构成压力。30年期美国国债收益率升至5.18%，创2007年以来新高。10年期美国国债收益率连续第三日上涨，收于2025年1月以来最高水平。

油价小幅走低，布伦特原油下跌0.7%至每桶111.28美元。此前特朗普总统表示，应海湾国家领导人请求，将暂缓对伊朗发动攻击。即便如此，基准布伦特原油价格过去一个月仍累计上涨逾20%。

CoreWeave股价下跌3.8%。《华尔街日报》报道称，Alphabet与黑石集团计划利用谷歌专用芯片成立一家人工智能云公司，与CoreWeave展开竞争。CoreWeave竞争对手Nebius股价亦下跌1%。

月度指数显示，4月份美国签约购房数量上升。作为基于合同签约量的房屋销售先行指标，成屋签约销售指数环比上升1.4%至74.8。《华尔街日报》调查的经济学家此前预计增幅为1%。
